hypotheses.reasoning: Until 13:24:40 every request was healthy (200s, health checks ok). The first anomaly is at #135, 13:24:55: template-svc gets a 503 from the third-party email provider api.mailer.example. More 502/503s from the provider follow (#138, #145, #146). The circuit breaker opens at a 99% failure rate (#148), and its half-open probes keep failing through 13:33 (#153, #190). That means the provider stayed down the whole time. notification-svc then gets 503s (circuit open) from template-svc (#158), and the gateway returns 503s on /v1/notify (#136 onward). There's no deploy or config change in the logs, and redis, the database and the worker look healthy. The GC pause (#54) and the TLS-expiry warning (#60) are unrelated.
The gateway and notification-svc errors are downstream effects that spread through the template-svc circuit breaker, but the fault starts at the external provider.

verdict.recommendedAction: Escalate to the email provider (api.mailer.example), check their status page, and send them the x-request-ids from the failed calls. To reduce impact: accept /v1/notify requests and queue the email sends for retry (async via notif-worker) instead of returning 503 synchronously, or switch to a backup email provider if one is configured. Leave the circuit breaker in place. Separately, renew the *.internal.example TLS certificate (it expires in 21 days).
